publish.title: Publish a provider
publish.intro: A successful endpoint check is not Hub registration. Follow these steps on the Hub you chose; no payment or publication happens on this page.
publish.prepare.title: Prepare the manifest
publish.prepare.body: Deploy the checked endpoint over HTTPS on port 443. Keep the signing key local. Set product_id, capability_id, provider_pubkey and price_per_call_usd in capability.json; use the exact schemas and endpoint you tested.
publish.identity.title: Confirm publisher identity
publish.identity.body: Open the Hub account page and create your own API key. Read account_id with the command below and use it as publisher_id in the manifest. Never share the API key or use an operator's admin token.
publish.stake.title: Review collateral separately
publish.stake.body: Ask the Hub operator for the current minimum collateral and admission policy before funding. Invocation credit and supplier collateral are different balances. Staking locks funds and may expose them to slashing. Obtain explicit approval for amount, source and recipient; do not treat a trial credit as sufficient collateral.
publish.register.title: Register explicitly
publish.register.body: After collateral and admission requirements are met, submit the manifest from your terminal. The command changes the Hub registry. It does not invoke the provider. An API-key account can only publish under its own account_id.
publish.discover.title: Verify discovery
publish.discover.body: Confirm the exact product_id, capability_id and provider_pubkey in the returned search results. An accepted registration is not a guarantee of discovery: trust and admission policy still apply.
publish.refusal.title: Resolve a refusal
publish.refusal.body: Do not retry payments or disable security gates to bypass a refusal. 401/403: check credentials and publisher identity; 402: check the returned collateral requirement; 503: ask the operator to restore admission services. Keep the response and check report, but remove secrets before sharing.
start.title: Developer workspace
start.snapshot: The archive contains a source snapshot from the generators or SDK, with SOURCES.json checksums. Dependencies install from package registries. No private keys are included. Commands use a macOS / Linux shell; on Windows use WSL. Extract the ZIP before running commands.
start.provider.summary: Your service, a declared contract, a request-bound signature. Start locally, then check the public endpoint.
start.provider.note1: Install dependencies and generate your Ed25519 identity. Keep .aimarket/provider.key private and back it up; capability.json contains only the public key.
start.provider.note2: Tests and the invoke profile run against your provider. Port 8080 must be free. check_local.py starts and stops the server, writes JSON to report.json and exits 0 only on a pass. The report is not signed by Hub.
start.provider.note3: The command starts a local server only. Deploy it behind an HTTPS ingress on port 443, preserve the private key, set invoke_url in capability.json and add access controls and rate limits. Then import the manifest into the public check. Never upload the private key.
start.provider.scope: Passing aimarket-provider-invoke/1 checks one invocation and its signature, not the entire protocol. It does not publish the capability or test Hub receipts, payments, discovery, federation, freshness or load. Publication requires a separate decision and the selected Hub's admission and stake rules.
start.provider.afterNote: After the public check, review publisher identity, price, input/output schemas and the Hub's publication admission requirements. Publish deliberately through Hub; this workspace never registers a service or moves funds.
start.consumer.summary: Discover a service, invoke with a price ceiling, inspect the receipt. The starter uses the GAIA weather fixture.
start.consumer.note1: Install dependencies and run the offline tests. The SDK snapshot is included: Python A2AClient or TypeScript market.run. No account or wallet is needed for discovery.
start.consumer.note2: Read-only discovery on modelmarket.dev. Inspect the GAIA weather offer and input.json. Only gaia.gateway / gaia.weather.read@v1 from iot.modelmarket.dev is eligible for this fixture. An unavailable offer stops the invocation.
start.consumer.note3: This command authorizes one real invocation, capped at $0.01. Without credentials it requests the Hub's limited trial; if AIMARKET_API_KEY is set locally, credits may be charged. Payment refusal, timeout or invalid receipt stops the run. There is no automatic top-up or retry.
start.consumer.scope: Python verifies receipt signatures locally against the origin key obtained over TLS. TypeScript requests verification from Hub and requires its live-key verdict. Neither proves the result is factually correct or pins identity independently. A successful run saves report.json. attempt.json blocks repeat runs, including after a lost response: reconcile the first attempt before removing it to authorize another charge.
start.consumer.afterNote: Replace the capability identifiers and input together after reviewing the service contract. Set a deliberate budget and keep credentials in your local environment. A provider can also be a consumer; the two roles are independent.
start.failed: Project could not be loaded. Reload the page to try again.
start.downloadFailed: Download or checksum verification failed. No file was saved; try again.
start.safety: Keys stay local. Publication and invocation are explicit actions.
meta.title: AIMarket Playground — First verified invoke
meta.description: Run a real AIMarket capability, inspect Metis verification, and receive a Hub receipt — no wallet or local cluster.
hero.title: Make the network
hero.lead: One real GAIA reading travels through the Hub, into a Metis verification gate, and comes back with a signed Hub receipt.
